news.title: APEC live: Trump arrives at resort for meetings with Xi, Putin
news.text:
SHENZHEN -- Chinese President Xi Jinping is hosting leaders including U.S. counterpart Donald Trump and Russia's Vladimir Putin at this year's Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum, showcasing his own country's technological prowess against a backdrop of cold and hot conflicts.

The proceedings in the southern tech hub of Shenzhen kicked off with a CEO Summit of business leaders on Tuesday, to be followed by an Economic Leaders' Meeting beginning Wednesday. On the sidelines, Xi and Trump are expected to have their third summit of the year as they seek to manage a fraught superpower rivalry.

As the Ukraine war drags on and tensions with Iran simmer, all eyes are on a trilateral summit among Xi, Trump and Putin that the White House has said will happen on Thursday. This prospect has drawn comparisons to the Yalta conference among the U.S., U.K. and Soviet Union to discuss the fate of postwar Europe in 1945.

Before departing for Asia on Monday, Trump told reporters that he might meet North Korean leader Kim Jong Un in China, a surprise announcement that could become another focal point of his visit.

Nikkei Asia is on the ground in Shenzhen to cover the meetings.

Further reading:

Here are the latest developments (Shenzhen time):

Thursday, Nov. 19

1:40 p.m. Trump and Xi pose in front of U.S. and Chinese flags for photos

1:30 p.m. Trump has arrived at the Kylin Villa, a lakeside resort in Shenzhen that will serve as the venue for his bilateral summit with Xi and the trilateral including Putin.

12:43 p.m. Trump met with Putin on the sidelines of the APEC forum following the plenary leaders session. Their meeting comes ahead a bilateral between Trump and Xi and a trilateral among the three leaders.

"We've had a great relationship for many years. We know each other for a long time, and I think a lot of wonderful things can come out of this, or at least start. But I think they'll come out of this," Trump told Putin.

1:30 p.m. Trump has arrived at the Kylin Villa, a lakeside resort in Shenzhen that will serve as the venue for his bilateral summit with Xi and the trilateral including Putin.

12:35 p.m. Elon Musk told an APEC organizer that he was a "super fan" of China, according to a social media post by Yuyuan Tiantian, an account affiliated with Chinese state broadcaster CCTV.

According to the post, the Tesla and SpaceX boss told Ren Hongbin, president of the China Council for the Promotion of International Trade, about his admiration for China's "magnificent buildings and natural landscapes" as well as its railway system.

Tesla will continue to increase production in China, Musk said, according to the post. He was photographed sitting in a room across Ren, wearing a black jacket, pants and shoes.

12:06 p.m. APEC plenary session ends

10:58 a.m. Putin tells his APEC counterparts that Russia contributes to regional energy security and that they can "always count on Moscow." He also invites all regional partners to use Russian logistics infrastructure.

10:39 a.m. Trump spoke about the U.S. economy and claimed his administration is taming inflation. He also said in his remarks that trade deals were forthcoming.

"The United States has been a Pacific power for hundreds of years, and we continue to work to promote growth and stability, sovereignty, prosperity, and peace throughout this region," he said.

Trump also said AI regulation needed to be carefully managed and opposed measures that would "stifle" the industry. "We won't allow that to happen," he said.

Trump said he looked forward to meeting with Xi and Putin later this afternoon. but did not elaborate. The trilateral will follow a two-way meeting between Xi and Trump, their third this year.

10:30 a.m. Putin is taking the opportunity presented by APEC to shore up ties with Asian partners. He and Vietnamese leader To Lam agreed to step up cooperation with "a focus on traditional and new energy, including nuclear power, wind power and gas-fired power," according to Vietnam's readout.

The statement also says they "underscored the importance of maintaining peace, security and stability, increasing dialogue and cooperation, and upholding the role of multilateralism, the United Nations and the fundamental principles of international law."

10:10 a.m. In his opening address, Xi called for cooperation on Al and supply chains. The Chinese president proposed building "four key pillars" for development in the Asia-Pacific: economy and trade, connectivity, innovation and development.

He said China will provide $20 million to support cooperation in areas such as digital technology and clean energy.

9:50 a.m. Xi has opened the leaders summit, with the visiting dignitaries gathered around circular tables in a large conference room under chandeliers. Moments before sitting down for the plenary session, they took a photo with Xi in the center, flanked by Putin and Trump. Takaichi was positioned in the back row to the side.

9:40 a.m. In an interview with Fox News, Trump said he spoke with Xi about artificial intelligence, and former Nvidia chief Jensen Huang only came up "briefly," Reuters reports.

"I haven't heard that she was a spy," Trump said, in reference to Huang's extramarital affair with Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang.

9:30 a.m. APEC leaders are gathering for the forum's main event, which begins with a "family photo" before they convene for the plenary session. Xi has urged his guests to pursue "concrete results" promoting economic openness and innovation, but time is limited. Attention in the afternoon will turn to the U.S.-China bilateral meeting and the highly anticipated Trump-Xi-Putin trilateral. There are reports that Trump will squeeze in a one-on-one meeting with Putin as well, although it is unclear how substantial that would be.

9:28 a.m. While we await today's events, here's some reading. A report to U.S. Congress on Wednesday by the U.S.-China Economic and Security Review Commission said that the unusually active" level of engagement between Trump and Xi is masking Beijing's ongoing efforts to outcompete America economically, technologically and militarily.

8:00 a.m. The most anticipated day of the APEC gathering is about to unfold. Looking at Trump's schedule, he will attend an APEC Leaders' Plenary Session at 09:45 a.m., followed by a bilateral with Xi and then a trilateral with Xi and Putin. We will also be looking out for other meetings on the sidelines. The wild card could be the arrival of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, but as always information out of the Hermit Kingdom is spotty.

12:10 a.m. Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi spoke with Russian President Vladimir Putin for about 30 minutes on the sidelines of the APEC summit and related meetings in Shenzhen, their countries' first face-to-face leaders' meeting since Russia invaded Ukraine in 2022.

According to the Japanese government's account of the talks, Takaichi pressed Putin to release a Japanese journalist detained for more than a month and reverse measures putting Japan Tobacco's Russian subsidiaries under local management. The two agreed to maintain communication at various levels.

Wednesday, Nov. 18

9:20 p.m. In a welcome speech at the banquet, Xi called on APEC leaders to work toward "concrete results" when they convene Thursday morning. He said they will discuss expanding mutual openness, explore paths for innovation-driven growth and broaden opportunities for practical cooperation across various sectors, state news agency Xinhua reports.

Xi said that since his first visit to Shenzhen in 1978, the small fishing village has become a "gateway for China's high-standard opening-up."

"Openness is in Shenzhen's DNA," he is quoted as saying.

9:00 p.m. Footage and photos coming out of the APEC leaders' banquet show some highly anticipated diplomatic interactions. Trump and Putin are seen shaking hands as Xi looks on, a prelude to Thursday's closely watched trilateral summit.

Xi also is pictured shaking hands with Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi. This was a major "will they or won't they" question ahead of the summit, as China-Japan ties have been frosty for over a year, since Takaichi spoke about a potential Taiwan crisis in the Japanese parliament. Takaichi is pictured smiling broadly at Xi after the greeting.

7:00 p.m. Chinese leader Xi Jinping and his wife, Peng Liyuan, are hosting a banquet at the Shenzhen International Exchange Center for APEC leaders. Live footage from state broadcaster CCTV shows U.S. President Donald Trump arriving at the venue.

6:00 p.m. South Korean President Lee Jae Myung held talks with Chinese leader Xi Jinping earlier amid speculation that Trump could meet North Korean leader Kim Jong Un in Shenzhen.

Xi told Lee he is willing to support "various efforts aimed at easing tensions on the Korean Peninsula, including a North Korea-U.S. dialogue," according to South Korean National Security Adviser Wi Sung-lac, as quoted by the Yonhap news agency.

Lee had asked China to play "a constructive role" in addressing Korean Peninsula issues, which the South Korean president described as a "do or die" matter, according to the same Yonhap report.

Chinese state-owned news outlet Xinhua made no mention of a potential Trump-Kim summit or of Korean Peninsula tensions in its account of the meeting published Wednesday afternoon.

Xi and Lee acknowledged that next year marks the 35th anniversary of their countries' diplomatic relations. Xinhua said Xi called the anniversary an opportunity to promote the steady development of their ties. Xi also mentioned that both countries are "beneficiaries of multilateralism and free trade," poking at a possible wedge between the U.S. and its key Asian ally, given Trump's tariff policies.

Lee called for strengthening the neighbors' relations "based on the mutual trust and friendship the two countries have built so far," referring to the anniversary, according to Yonhap.

5:05 p.m. Xi greets Trump on the tarmac, reciprocating a rare airport welcome that Trump afforded him when he visited Washington in September. Ties between the rival superpowers have grown increasingly tense in recent weeks over tech restrictions and other contentious points, but the Shenzhen gathering provides the two leaders an opportunity to maintain their fragile trade truce. At the airport, the atmosphere appears friendly, with the presidents chatting and smiling before making their way past an honor guard and a welcome crew waving Chinese and American flags.

Xi stands and waves as Trump departs in his black limo, known as the Beast.

4:45 p.m. Trump lands in Shenzhen. TV footage shows Air Force One taxiing at the airport.

3:30 p.m. Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese reveals in remarks to CEOs that he spoke with Xi about his first visit to Shenzhen back in 1998, when he was a young politician. Back then, the city was still a long way away from becoming the tech hub it is today.

"You don't think of it as a same place," he said. Like Thailand's Anutin immediately before him, Albanese called Shenzhen an example of the region's success.

3:00 p.m. Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul recounts how Chinese Premier Li Qiang "kept telling me the story of Shenzhen" when they met in Bangkok on Friday, about how a fishing village four decades ago became a global business metropolis.

Anutin said he interpreted the story of the APEC host city as an example of how a "transformation can be achieved where an economy opens itself up."

The Thai leader touted the benefits of Thailand's preparations to join the Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development. "Our OECD accession process is helping improve governance and regulatory standards and transparency," he said.

Regarding online scam groups that are active especially in Thailand's border regions with Myanmar and Cambodia, Anutin stresses that there is a "global partnership" to fight cross-border organized crime.

2:15 p.m. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney tells APEC's business gathering that his country is taking "practical steps" with China on financial cooperation, including for times of stress. He also cites growing collaboration in the green economy sector, crediting China's wind and solar industries for the opportunities they create.

Carney -- whose government has faced friction with the U.S. under Trump despite the neighbors' traditionally tight ties -- has made a point this year to improve relations with China.

Praising the Chinese leadership that turned Shenzhen into a tech hub, he said, "The choices that built this city will lift this whole region." And he says that "Canada has made our choice to build a more stronger, prosperous and a more sovereign future."

Carney alluded to geopolitical tensions, saying "it's no insight to say that this has been a difficult year for international consensus." However, he said, APEC is delivering on tangible cooperation.

12:00 p.m. South Korean President Lee Jae Myung meets with Xi on the sidelines, and tells him that he wants to work together to promote peace and stability on the Korean Peninsula, according to the media pool. Xi tells his guest that he is willing to work with South Korea on preserving stable industrial supply chains.

Their meeting comes amid growing rumblings that North Korean leader Kim Jong Un could make an appearance at APEC to meet with some attendees, including Trump. U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio told reporters earlier in Manila that Trump is "serious" about engaging with Kim and "prepared to do it," although he acknowledged that a meeting might not materialize.

11:30 a.m. Russian President Vladimir Putin piles on with implicit criticism of the U.S., saying that "former dominant powers" have tried to suppress the development of other countries.

"Economic domination and coercion are now a thing of the past," he says, praising nations that have preserved their own identities and independence and arguing that sanctions and tariffs have not held Russia back.

He hails Shenzhen as a "modern vibrant megacity" and a symbol of tech, economic and social transformation in China and Asia. The region, he says, is setting an example of a "more fair, democratic and equal world order."

Putin also says he expects significant benefits from his upcoming trilateral meeting with Xi and Trump.

11:15 a.m. Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim is the next to address business leaders after China's Xi. While praising the host several times, Anwar delivers thinly veiled criticism of the U.S., without naming it directly. He stresses the importance of free and open business activity, emphasizing, "You can't say in one voice [that you're] promoting trade and investment, but only to your country."

11:10 a.m. Stan Shih, the founder of computer maker Acer and Taiwan's representative to the APEC summit, says he will "actively" engage with other members in Shenzhen as he departs from Taipei, according to Reuters.

APEC is one of the few international organizations that includes Taiwan, which participates as "Chinese Taipei." The administration is sending Shih in lieu of President Lai Ching-te, who Beijing considers a "separatist" because he rejects its territorial claim to Taiwan.

Shih describes Taiwan as a "trustworthy" player in the region and an indispensable partner for the global technology and AI sectors. He vows to "show the international community Taiwan's strength and contributions."

"Taiwan will go with a smile," he says.

10:10 a.m. Xi addresses the APEC CEO Summit, his first time to do so in person since 2018 in Papua New Guinea. Positioning himself as an advocate for stability, he called for resolving differences through dialogue and for defending free and open trade. He is discussing the dilemmas economies face between being open or closed, between cooperation and division and between change or taking a conservative approach. "These are all questions of our time that we must answer," he said.

9:45 a.m. The second day of APEC proceedings is about to get underway. Putin landed in Shenzhen overnight, while Trump is expected to fly in later in the day, as is Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi. A number of leaders, including Xi and Putin, are due to deliver speeches to business participants, with more bilateral mettings on the sidelines.

Tuesday, Nov. 17

5:30 p.m. Xi continues his day of meetings with visiting leaders, sitting down separately with Mexico's Claudia Sheinbaum, Peru's Keiko Fujimori and Chile's Jose Antonio Kast.

Mexico last year riled China by approving higher tariffs on countries with which it does not have trade deals, affecting hundreds of products. The move was widely seen as an effort to close a "back door" to the U.S.

Sheinbaum told Xi she is eager to step up cooperation with China in areas related to technology, agriculture, water, health and tourism, according to Reuters.

4:30 p.m. Speculation that North Korean leader Kim Jong Un could appear at APEC and meet with Trump continues to grow. Russia's Interfax news agency has cited the Kremlin as saying that Putin could also meet Kim if he shows up in Shenzhen, adding weight to the prospect of a Kim visit.

Shortly before he departed the U.S. for Asia, Trump himself suggested that a meeting with Kim could happen. Trump met Kim three times during his first presidency and has expressed interest in a reunion.

3:30 p.m. BYD Chairman and President Wang Chuanfu says on a panel that the electric carmaker's Thailand and Indonesia plants have created 6,000 local jobs each and nearly all of its employees at the factories are local hires.

"Our goal is not merely to export Chinese technology globally; we also aim to generate local employment and tax revenue, fostering mutually beneficial cooperation and win-win outcomes," he said.

Wang added that its Thailand factory sources just over half of components domestically.

His comments come as a rush of Chinese vehicle exports stokes trade tensions with some partner economies.

2:00 p.m. Papua New Guinea Prime Minister James Marape has assured Xi that Taiwan no longer operates in his country. PNG pushed for the closure of Taipei's representative office in its capital, Port Moresby, and Taiwan announced earlier this month that it would indeed shut down the mission.

Marape told Xi that he hopes the move "assists you in your efforts for reunification," referring to China's claim to Taiwan, which the administration in Taipei rejects.

Taiwan had been a major buyer of gas from PNG, but said it would halt spot purchases in reaction to the closure. China, in turn, committed to increasing its purchases.

12:30 p.m. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said there is now "greater predictability and stability" in his country's ties with China, as he met Chinese President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen. Xi said that since the two leaders agreed to promote a strategic partnership back in January, exchanges and cooperation between China and Canada have fully resumed.

Carney's visit to Beijing in January thawed a relationship that had been severely strained in recent years, especially after the 2018 detention of Huawei executive Meng Wanzhou in Canada and the subsequent jailing of two Canadians on espionage charges -- all of whom were eventually released.

A statement released by Carney's office about Tuesday's meeting says that Canada "has recalibrated our relationship with China -- strategically, pragmatically, and decisively." It also says the two sides agreed to extend and expand a preliminary agreement to address trade issues, opening up greater access to the Chinese market for Canada's farmers and seafood harvesters and securing more tariff relief for about 400 million Canadian dollars ($280 million) worth of exports.

The statement also mentions a slew of other initiatives to boost trade, e-commerce, educational exchanges and air travel.

11:30 a.m. Trump's Air Force One made a refueling stop in Alaska before a layover in the Philippines, where Manila is hosting ASEAN leaders and related summits.

Before leaving Washington, Trump said he might meet North Korean leader Kim Jong Un in China. The hermit nation is not a member of APEC and South Korean officials played down the possibility of such a meeting, Yonhap News Agency reported on Nov. 11.

Trump's planned attendance at APEC contrasts with last year's summit in Gyeongju, South Korea, when he met Xi Jinping in Busan and secured a trade truce but left before the main agenda began. His Shenzhen engagement signals an effort to keep ties with Xi on track ahead of next month's G20 Summit in Miami, where they are expected to meet again.

9:30 a.m. Beijing has yet to formally respond to Washington's latest move to tighten China's access to advanced artificial intelligence chips through overseas data centers. Vice Premier He Lifeng raised concerns over U.S. restrictions on China in a phone call earlier this month.

The broader AI boom is also rattling markets. Shenzhen's tech-heavy ChiNext Index sank 4.4% on Monday to a nearly 16-month low, led by steep losses among suppliers to AI data centers. U.S. stocks also fell sharply ahead of Nvidia's earnings on Tuesday.

9:00 a.m. Foreign leaders are trickling into Shenzhen. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum and Papua New Guinea Prime Minister James Marape arrived on Monday, according to Chinese media.

The leaders are expected to hold bilateral meetings with Xi on Tuesday, according to media reports. Carney is visiting China for the second time this year. In January, he met with Xi and lowered Canada's tariff wall on Chinese electric vehicles by setting up an import quota. Among the topics expected to be discussed during his visit to Shenzhen is Chinese investment into Canada's auto sector.

Trade tensions loom over Sheinbaum's visit, after she raised import tariffs on cars, textiles, appliances and other items from countries without free trade agreements with Mexico, including China. In addition to meeting Xi, she is expected to speak at the CEO Summit on Tuesday.
news.author: Wataru Suzuki

news.title: Trump and Xi hold 3rd summit of year as friendly vibes mask deep divisions
news.text: SHENZHEN -- Chinese President Xi Jinping met with U.S. counterpart Donald Trump for the third time this year on Thursday, as the two leaders sought to maintain a shaky trade truce due to expire in January.
news.author: Kenji Kawase

news.title: Trump and Putin hold first meeting since August 2025
news.text:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, November 19. Russian
President Vladimir Putin met with US President Donald Trump after
the plenary session of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC)
summit, the Kremlin press service announced.

Russia was represented at the talks by Foreign Minister Sergey
Lavrov, Finance Minister Anton Siluanov, Presidential Aide Yuri
Ushakov, and Kirill Dmitriev, CEO of the Russian Direct Investment
Fund and the Russian president's special representative for
investment and economic cooperation with foreign countries.

The US delegation included Secretary of State and Acting
National Security Adviser Marco Rubio, as well as Treasury
Secretary Scott Bessent.

The meeting marks the presidents' first bilateral talks since
their negotiations in Anchorage, Alaska, in August 2025.
news.author: Vugar Ismayilov

news.title: Putin is my friend; we look forward to our meeting: Trump before China talks
news.text: Digital Desk | Washington, Nov 19 (IANS) US President Donald Trump met Russian President Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen on Thursday, calling him a "friend" and expressing hope for progress ahead of a scheduled three-way meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping. The encounter took place on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation leaders' gathering. "Who is he? He's my friend," Trump said before the meeting. "We look forward to our meeting. We've had a great relationship for many years," he said. "I think a lot of wonderful things can come out of this, or at least start," Trump added, referring also to a second meeting later in the day. The pool reports available at the time of writing did not disclose the substance or outcome of the discussions. Trump did not identify any specific agreement in his opening remarks. The US President entered the meeting room at about 12:15 p.m. local time, or 9:45 a.m. in India. He immediately shook Putin's hand, according to television footage. Putin also shook hands with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent before the discussions, the subsequent report said. The meeting was held in a separate room within the conference centre used for the APEC plenary. A different group of reporters was waiting at Shenzhen's Kylin Villa, a government reception compound, for Trump's bilateral meeting with Xi and the subsequent three-way talks. China's Foreign Ministry had announced on November 16 that Xi would hold a China-Russia-US summit with Trump and Putin in Shenzhen on November 19. Earlier on Thursday, Trump addressed the APEC leaders' plenary, where he said he looked forward to meeting Xi and Putin but did not elaborate on the discussions. The separate encounter with Putin provided an opportunity for the US and Russian leaders to speak before joining their Chinese counterpart.
news.author: IANS News

news.title: Azeri Light falls below $98 per barrel at Italian port
news.text:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, November 19. The price of
Azerbaijan's Azeri Light crude oil on a CIF basis at Italy's
Augusta port fell by $1.17, or 1.2%, from the previous figure to
$97.62 per barrel, oil market participants said.

At Türkiye's Ceyhan port, the price of Azeri Light on a FOB
basis decreased by $1.28, or 1.3%, to $93.65 per barrel.

The price of Russia's Urals crude fell by $1.09, or 1.6%, to
$67.93 per barrel.

North Sea Dated Brent crude was down by $1.04, or 1.1%, at
$92.11 per barrel.

Azerbaijan's state budget for 2026 assumes an average oil price
of $65 per barrel.

According to the latest data from Trading Economics, Brent crude
prices hovered around $92 per barrel on Thursday, remaining near
their lowest levels since late August. Expectations of a
significant global supply surplus outweighed renewed geopolitical
tensions in the Middle East.

According to the US Energy Information Administration (EIA), US
commercial crude oil inventories rose by 3.38 million barrels in
the week ended November 13, reaching 417.8 million barrels. The
previous week saw an increase of 4.657 million barrels.

Gasoline inventories also increased by 5.192 million barrels,
while distillate fuel inventories rose by 1.571 million

Meanwhile, the International Energy Agency forecasts a global
oil supply surplus of around 2 million barrels per day in the
current quarter. Goldman Sachs has also warned of a possible supply
glut next year, Trading Economics reported.

Oil prices have fallen by around 20% since the beginning of the
month amid the recovery of supplies from the Middle East, despite
intermittent regional tensions. Meanwhile, US President Donald
Trump has refrained from launching large-scale military strikes
against Iran.
news.author: Aytaj Shiraliyeva

news.title: Burke backtracks on backpacker changes as PM is cheered on world stage
news.text:
You could fill more than a couple of backpacks with all the backtracks the government has been doing of late — and this time it was Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke's turn.

The Labor stalwart smiled as he did his best to spin his changes to the changes on backpacker policy.

He back-pedalled on plans to slash the numbers of working holiday maker visas and lifted a proposed cap on third-year visas, while also increasing the number of days foreigners must work in the regions to be eligible.

He also delayed the introduction of a ballot system until March, and it has now been rebranded as a "ballot-style" system called the Next Year Regional Work Guarantee, after pressure from the agriculture, tourism and hospitality sectors.

Burke argued a go-slow to visa processing earlier this year gave him the headroom to make the tweaks, insisting it wouldn't impact the guarantee he made back in September that the government was definitely going to reduce Australia's net overseas migration. In other words, Labor is on track to achieve its targets because Home Affairs is processing visas really, really slowly.

Of course, the government would argue it's hardly uncommon to change its position. As Murray Watt argued when pressed on the backpacker visa changes: "You put out a proposal, you then talk about it with the stakeholders, and you arrive at a final landing spot, and that's what we've been able to do here."

Others, such as Greens leader David Shoebridge, argued that's a back-to-front approach.

"I've got some advice for the government: maybe before you have your next brain fart, go out and talk to the community, see who's going to be impacted and do that before you make the announcement," he said.

The backpacker backtrack is not the first. The Albanese government has been quick to shelve issues before they become too much of a political problem. There's been the scrapping of the veterans' allied health cap, the ATO credit card ban, the sale of four defence sites, just to name a few over recent months.

But all of this chopping and changing does have an impact on the budget bottom line — something the government has its eyes on as the Mid-Year Economic and Fiscal Outlook draws closer.

Trusts and the guillotine

Treasurer Jim Chalmers returned to the spotlight this week after a fortnight in the dark (I mean this literally — he posted a video of himself driving around in the dark to Instagram after storms hit his electorate).

Chalmers delivered a speech to an ASIC forum where he repeated much of what he's already said: there will be savings in the budget. As reporters questioned him, he also insisted he would remain treasurer until the next election.

The budget headaches go beyond just MYEFO for Chalmers as the status of his budget tax changes — the capital gains discount and a minimum 30 per cent tax on discretionary trusts — continues to be a thorn in the government's side.

Neither were dealt with during the Senate-only sitting week. When the guillotine motion — which cuts off debate to force votes on a number of bills — was put forward on Thursday afternoon, it was clear a deal was still yet to be done.

The Coalition remains "dead against" both. So that leaves the Greens as the only path forward. The minor party floated the idea of sending the CGT changes off to yet another inquiry as it publicly flirted with Allegra Spender's alternative idea.

If the CGT changes did go to an inquiry, that would delay its passage until next year — something the government really doesn't want. It's likely the Greens will end up passing both bills next week with some amendments.

Cook-ing with gas (reservation scheme)

Between the casting of James Bond (spare a thought for Don Farrell, who seemed willing to trade his moniker as the Godfather for Bond), the release of GTA 6 and Sandpapergate, if your attention wasn't on the Senate only sitting week… that's so fair.

So, what happened? Not much.

The tax bills weren't dealt with, and neither was the gas reservation scheme. The proposal would require Australia's largest gas exports to set aside up to 20 per cent of its exports for domestic supply. An unlikely alliance of unions and industry groups called for the parliament to pass it this week.

Western Australia had been the big sticking point here. The state has its own scheme set up and has been arguing for a carve-out to be baked in, rather than through ministerial discretion. Premier Roger Cook (it's always him, hey), struck a last-minute deal.

All eyes are now on the Coalition. Opposition Leader Angus Taylor indicated early in the week that WA was the key block to the party's support. But other conditions include greater limits on ministerial powers, concerns about deliberate oversupply and the removal of the "must sell" rule on producers.

It also wasn't put up for a vote on Thursday, dragging the issue into next week alongside CGT, trusts, and private health insurance rebate changes.

Pom-pom and ceremony

What do a chicken shop in Manila and rows of pom-pom wielding cheerleaders have in common? Anthony Albanese.

The prime minister headed overseas again. This time his schedule took him to the Philippines for ASEAN, where the Quad leaders — which includes US President Donald Trump, Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi — met for the first time in two years.

Trump's assessment of the group? Modi was "a very tough man" but Takaichi "may be even tougher". As for the PM, well, "We're okay," he said before giving him a slap on the back.

An agreement to conduct a joint military exercise and to cooperate on critical minerals were the key takeaways from the meeting that took place before they jetted off to APEC in Shenzhen, China.

While Albanese was greeted by cheerleaders, President Xi Jinping welcomed Trump with a hug on the tarmac. The pair will be joined by Russian President Vladmir Putin for a trilateral meeting on Thursday afternoon.

Ahead of the meeting, Albanese called the dialogue a "good thing".

"At a time when there are more conflicts than at any time since the Second World War … we want to see more dialogue, less military conflict," he said.

The PM is set to have his own talks with Xi on the sidelines of APEC on Friday. It'll act as a primer for talks when parliament returns next week for the final sitting week of the year.
news.summary: While Anthony Albanese has been doing the rounds of global summits, his government is facing a grilling on budget measures it's trying to get through the Senate.
news.author: Courtney Gould

news.title: Federal workers warned not to telework for Grand Theft Auto VI
news.text:
The Trump administration on Wednesday playfully warned federal workers that the release of the highly anticipated video game Grand Theft Auto VI does not count as a valid excuse to work from home.

“Reminder: GTA6 coming out is not a basis for situational telework!” the Office of Personnel Management said in a cheeky social media post, acknowledging the seismic buzz over the game’s release.

Players have been waiting more than a decade for the new open-world action title from Rockstar Games, which officially comes out on Nov. 19.

It’s already become the best-reviewed video game ever, getting a 99/100 on the review aggregator Metacritic and a 98/100 on OpenCritic as the top-scoring game on both. Gaming websites IGN and GameSpot each gave GTA VI a perfect 10.

The lighthearted tweet from OPM comes as the administration has kept up pressure on federal employees to work at the office. President Donald Trump ordered US government workers back to their offices shortly after returning to the White House in 2025, moving to unwind telework arrangements that had become widespread during the Covid-19 pandemic.

Earlier: To Make ‘Grand Theft Auto VI,’ Rockstar Games Remade Itself 

Bloomberg’s review of the new Grand Theft Auto, called it a “masterpiece.” Some analysts expect the game to sell 40 million copies on PlayStation and Xbox and generate more than $3 billion in revenue in its first four months. 

The game took eight years to develop — and the efforts of more than 4,700 people. 

More stories like this are available on bloomberg.com

news.title: Trump surges to the top of Chinese social media just by showing up
news.text: President Donald Trump has become the hottest topic on China's social media this week — simply by dint of appearing in the country. Posts on Weibo, a major Chinese social media platform similar to X, discussing the president's visit to Shenzhen this week cumulatively hit over 200 million views by Thursday noon, local time. He arrived at the Chinese tech hub on Wednesday evening for the annual Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation, or APEC, summit, hosted by Chinese leader Xi Jinping. On Weibo, people uploaded photos and videos of Shenzhen residents gathering near road barricades to snap selfies or record clips of the presidential motorcade whizzing by. One topic — covering Xi's red-carpet welcome for Air Force One — surged to the top of Weibo on Wednesday evening, receiving 120 million views. "The fan support is wild," one blogger wrote. "Trump has beaten the entire Chinese entertainment industry." Memes and lighthearted jokes flooded the site, which, like all official Chinese social media platforms, is heavily moderated under Beijing's guidance. Some posted blurry photos of Trump looking out the window of his presidential limousine, "The Beast," taking it as a sign he was admiring Shenzhen. Trump, who's been a cult figure in China even while out of office, received a similarly viral following on its social media when he visited Beijing in May. The hashtag #TrumpVisitsChina garnered 210 million visits within a day of his arrival that month. His predecessor, President Joe Biden, never visited China during his stint in the White House. Trump is set to meet both Xi and his Russian counterpart, Vladimir Putin, this week in a high-stakes trilateral meeting as tensions between their nations continue to grow. A major topic on the agenda for the trio is nuclear arms reduction, while Trump has said he intends to also raise the issue of Ukraine at the meeting, though White House officials later said it was not planned for discussion.Tesla CEO and SpaceX founder Elon Musk is also joining Trump for parts of his trip to China. Musk, whose companies have significant business interests in China, is not expected to take part in the official meetings. It is the third time Trump and Xi have met in person this year, with a fourth meeting planned at December's G20 summit in Miami. The White House did not immediately respond to a comment request sent outside regular business hours by Business Insider.
news.summary: Trump, a cult figure in China, blasted to the top of Weibo's trending topics this week. All he had to was arrive.
news.author: Matthew Loh

news.title: VIDEO: Putin’s nuclear briefcase caught on camera in China
news.text:
The nuclear briefcase of Russian President Vladimir Putin was spotted on camera in a rare appearance on Wednesday ahead of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen, China.

The summit marks a historic formal trilateral meeting to be held among Putin, his US counterpart Donald Trump and China’s Xi Jinping.

In footage released by Russian state TV and posted by CBS News on its Facebook page late Wednesday, a Russian journalist was seen approaching a Russian naval officer who confirmed the briefcase’s identity.

Before approaching the officer, the journalist said, while the camera was focused on the officer and some unknown men, “Look, that’s the famous nuclear briefcase right behind us.”

He then walked up to the officer and asked, “Hello, is this the nuclear briefcase you’ve got there?”

The officer replied, with a smile on his face, “Yes.”

In what looked like a further confirmation, the journalist queried further, “Yes? The one?”

“The one,” the officer affirmed, while walking in a direction that was not shown on camera.

Showing an element of surprise after the brief interview, the journalist said, “Unbelievable!”

Known as the “Cheget,” CBS News reports that the briefcase allows Putin to “maintain unbroken command and control over Russia’s nuclear arsenal at all times, regardless of his physical location.”

Fox News said the briefcase “reportedly travels with Putin at all times, but it’s rarely seen on camera,” while Al Jazeera stated that the briefcase can be used to “authorise a nuclear strike.” 

Beijing has long maintained that the US and Russia should reduce their giant nuclear arsenals before it agrees to talks on its smaller stockpile, PUNCH Online reports Wednesday.

The report noted that the summit is expected to include discussions of the Iran war and nuclear disarmament, according to Washington, after a US-Russia bilateral treaty on atomic weapons expired in February.

Putin has been largely shunned by the West since his 2022 offensive in Ukraine began.

Earlier, the Russian leader informed the APEC gathering that what’s needed is “unity rather than division… and dialogue rather than ultimatums,” at a time when military and political tensions are “on the rise.”

Ukraine’s Foreign Minister Andriy Sybiga, speaking to reporters in Kyiv, said he hoped Xi and Trump would put “pressure on Russia to end the war.”

In his remarks, according to Chinese state news agency Xinhua. Xi told Trump that he looks forward to an “in-depth exchange of views with you on major issues concerning China-US relations, Asia-Pacific cooperation, and the global landscape, with the aim of advancing a constructive, strategically stable relationship between our two nations.”

news.title: Putin-Trump meeting lasts less than hour
news.text:
SHENZHEN /China/, November 19. /TASS/. The meeting between Russian President Vladimir Putin and his US counterpart Donald Trump on the sidelines of the APEC summit lasted less than an hour, a TASS correspondent reported.

It began at approximately 12:15 p.m. local time (4:15 a.m. GMT). The White House press pool announced its conclusion around 5:00 a.m. GMT.

This was the eighth face-to-face meeting between the Russian and US leaders during Trump’s two presidential terms. It is the second since Trump returned to the White House. The last time the Russian and US leaders met was 15 months ago in Anchorage.

news.title: Yankees great Mark Teixeira celebrates wildly after drawing LAST pick in House freshman office lottery
news.text:
Congressman-elect Mark Teixeira managed to garner applause from both Republicans and Democrats on Capitol Hill with his enthusiastic response to the office lottery pool. 

With 105 incoming representatives set to convene for the start of the 120th United States Congress on January 3, new members gathered for a 'freshman orientation' this week highlighted by Tuesday's office lottery. 

Each of the 105 members-elect drew a number from a wooden box to determine the order by which they would pick work spaces in the 233-year-old building. That 105th selection ultimately went to Teixeira, who proudly announced the number to the applauding members-elect on Tuesday. 

Teixeira, 46, soaked up the moment even further by raising his hands in the air and slowly turning to the crowd in a conspicuous departure from his days as a mild-mannered, power-hitting All-Star.

'The House office lottery was today, and I drew 105 out of 105,' the Republican from Texas' 21st district wrote on X. 'I consider it an honor to have the last pick of offices and let all my fellow freshmen go ahead of me.'

Teixeira then dropped a favorite verse from the New Testament: 'As Matthew 19:30 reminds us, "But many who are first will be last, and the last first."'

The 104-member wait meant Teixeira had more than 10 hours before he could pick an office.

Teixeira poured $2.5 million of his own MLB fortune into his bid to replace Chip Roy in Congress.

The Texas Tribune reported in February he raised more cash than any other candidate after loaning millions to his campaign and pulling in an extra $545,000 from donors before earning the endorsements of Donald Trump and Texas Governor Greg Abbott to be the Republican candidate.

And on a night that saw Abbott taken down by Democrat Gina Hinojosa in a stunning upset, Teixeira at least earned his spot to replace Roy by beating Democratic candidate Kristin Hook.

Teixeira was always favorite to win the Republican stronghold, which has been held by Rep. Roy since 2019 before he chose not to seek a fifth term in order to try and become Texas Attorney General.

The Maryland native played five brilliant seasons for the Texas Rangers before moving on to Atlanta, Anaheim and ultimately the Bronx, where he'd win a World Series and lead the American League in home runs in 2009.

Ultimately injuries abruptly ended his career at age 36 in 2016. Since then, the married father has worked as an MLB analyst for ESPN.

As for his interest in playing in the annual congressional baseball game, Teixeira may take a pass on suiting up for the GOP. 

As he wrote on X: 'I appreciate everyone asking if I'll play in the Congressional Baseball game, but it's not on my list of priorities. The good people of Texas' 21st District sent me to Washington to work for them. That's where my focus is, and I'm looking forward to getting to work!
news.summary: Congressman-elect Mark Teixeira managed to garner applause from both Republicans and Democrats on Capitol Hill with his enthusiastic response to the office lottery pool.
news.author: Alex Raskin,Editor

news.title: APEC Summit: Trump holds bilateral meeting with Putin ahead of trilateral talks
news.text: SHENZHEN: US President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin held a bilateral meeting on Thursday on the sidelines of the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders’ Meeting in Shenzhen, ahead of their anticipated trilateral talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping. Before leaving for Asia, Trump told reporters that discussions with Putin and Xi would address denuclearisation, Iran, trade, and the Russia-Ukraine conflict."We'll also talk about my favourite subject, Ukraine. Ukraine is losing. Ukraine and Russia are losing 25,000 souls per month, so we'll be talking about that. We'll also discuss economics and trade," Trump said..The proposed trilateral engagement comes at a sensitive moment for global arms control following the expiration of the US-Russia New START treaty in February 2026. While Trump hopes to negotiate a new nuclear framework that includes China, Beijing has previously resisted joining such talks, citing the significantly larger nuclear stockpiles maintained by the United States and Russia.Ahead of Trump’s arrival, Xi and Putin held bilateral talks and a working breakfast in Shenzhen on Wednesday, reaffirming their strategic partnership. Xi described China-Russia ties as "firm as a mountain amid wind and rain" and urged both powers to advance a multipolar world order.Putin noted that bilateral political cooperation was working constructively and told the APEC CEO Summit that tariffs, sanctions, and export curbs cannot halt the growth of emerging economies. He also expressed hope that the trilateral talks would prove of "great use.".Speaking at the APEC summit on Thursday, Xi called for free and open trade, smart customs systems, and inclusive regional cooperation, warning against protectionist barriers and technology restrictions. China has described the upcoming trilateral talks as holding "ground-breaking significance."(With inputs from agencies)

news.title: India flags Pakistan's mineral loot at UN, cites Asim Munir's display to Trump
news.text: India launched a blistering attack on the Pakistani military at the United Nations, accusing it of plundering the country's natural wealth for its own benefit. Speaking at a UN session on natural resources, India's envoy Parvathaneni Harish, without naming Donald Trump, pointed to Pakistan army chief Asim Munir's meeting with "foreign leaders", where he displayed a box filled with mineral stones. He said it exposed the Pakistan army's direct involvement in resource exploitation."Pakistan army chief was seen last September displaying a wooden box filled with mineral stones to foreign leaders, a clear indication of their army's role in (natural resource) exploitation," Harish said. He also took a potshot at the power structure in Islamabad, underlining that Pakistanis would be served better if their "real rulers" used the resources for the benefit of its citizens rather than for "self-aggrandisement"."Pakistanis would be served well if its real rulers, its military, used the country's natural resources for the benefit of their population rather than self-aggrandisement," the Indian envoy asserted. THE TRUMP-ASIM MUNIR MEETINGThe Indian envoy's reference was to a photo released by the White House last year during Trump's meeting with Munir and Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif.The photo showed Munir, Pakistan's de facto leader, presenting a wooden box containing rare earth minerals as Trump looks on keenly. The real leader, Sharif, is seen peeking from the sidelines.The optics, however, invited ridicule back home. A Pakistani senator likened Munir's gesture to a shopkeeper showing off merchandise to a customer. From army chief to "salesman-in-chief", mocked social media.The meeting came as Pakistan sought to cash in on its newfound bonhomie with Trump to attract American investment in its largely untapped mineral reserves.That same month, Pakistan's military-linked Frontier Works Organisation signed a USD 500 million deal with US Strategic Metals to explore strategic minerals in Pakistan for defence and technology use.In October 2025, Pakistan delivered its first-ever shipment of rare earth and critical minerals to the US, with the opposition questioning the secrecy of the deal.This is exactly what Indian envoy Harish sought to point out in his UN speech - the Pakistani military's direct involvement in the country's mineral wealth.INDIA RAKES UP EMERGENCY RULE IN KPHarish also sought to link the military's direct involvement in resource exploitation to the imposition of emergency rule in restive Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP).Last month, the Pakistani government imposed governor's rule in KP, where Imran Khan's PTI was in power, citing growing incidents of terrorism.What is also true is that the province has significant mineral deposits, including gold. Disputes over control of its natural resources have been a longstanding source of political friction in the region.Recently, Pakistan's KP governor suspended gold mining leases across the province amid allegations of illegal mining."The army's role in this exploitation... is also believed to be behind the recent dismissal of a provincial government in Pakistan and the imposition of a state of emergency there," Harish said.Drawing a sharp contrast with India, Harish said the country's mining laws require companies to fund local community development. He also underlined that lasting peace only happens when locals directly profit from the wealth extracted from their land.- EndsMust Watch
news.summary: India flags Pakistan's mineral loot at UN, cites Asim Munir's display to Trump

news.title: Ukraine attacked the Crimean Bridge for the third time since the beginning of the week
news.text:
On the night of November 19, Ukraine attacked the Crimean Bridge for the third time since the beginning of the week. "Traffic is temporarily blocked. All emergency services are on site. An assessment of the damage is underway," wrote the Russian-installed head of the peninsula, Sergei Aksyonov.

According to the Ukrainian monitoring channel Exilenova+, the strike on the crossing was carried out with missiles.

In turn, another Ukrainian channel, "Crimean Wind", claims that two hits struck the railway section of the bridge. As of the time of publication, there are no photos or videos confirming this.

Prior to this, the Armed Forces of Ukraine (AFU) struck the bridge on the nights of November 16 and 17. Following the first attack, the 227-meter arch of the road section of the crossing shifted by 15 degrees due to a drone hit, the Moscow Times writes.

After the second attack, which involved "Flamingo" cruise missiles, the arch collapsed into the water along with the roadway. The Exilenova+ channel published a video of the destruction taken from a train passing along the surviving railway track. Fire Point, the manufacturer of the "Flamingo", claimed that the strike destroyed more than 270 meters of the roadway. The attack on the bridge took place ahead of a trilateral meeting of the leaders of Russia, the United States, and China—Vladimir Putin, Donald Trump, and Xi Jinping—on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen.

Following the collapse of the Crimean Bridge arch, the government held an emergency meeting to discuss its restoration. Deputy Prime Minister Andrey Nikitin stated that the repair work could be completed in "a short time," but did not provide a specific date.

Former Verkhovna Rada deputy and former advisor to the Minister of Internal Affairs of Ukraine Anton Gerashchenko noted that restoring the bridge is impossible because marine cranes are needed for its repair, but Ukraine will not allow vessels to remain in the area and carry out the work. Emil Kastehelmi, an analyst with the Finnish OSINT project Black Bird Group, also wrote that the road bridge cannot be restored before the end of the war.

Meanwhile, according to data from the Vesselfinder service highlighted by "Verstka", six tugboats, a dredging vessel, and a ship designed for oil spill response arrived at the site of the bridge arch collapse. Judging by their movements, they were conducting work at the scene.

news.title: APEC live: Trump tells Putin 'We've had a great relationship for many years'
news.text:
SHENZHEN -- Chinese President Xi Jinping is hosting leaders including U.S. counterpart Donald Trump and Russia's Vladimir Putin at this year's Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum, showcasing his own country's technological prowess against a backdrop of cold and hot conflicts.

The proceedings in the southern tech hub of Shenzhen kicked off with a CEO Summit of business leaders on Tuesday, to be followed by an Economic Leaders' Meeting beginning Wednesday. On the sidelines, Xi and Trump are expected to have their third summit of the year as they seek to manage a fraught superpower rivalry.

As the Ukraine war drags on and tensions with Iran simmer, all eyes are on a trilateral summit among Xi, Trump and Putin that the White House has said will happen on Thursday. This prospect has drawn comparisons to the Yalta conference among the U.S., U.K. and Soviet Union to discuss the fate of postwar Europe in 1945.

Before departing for Asia on Monday, Trump told reporters that he might meet North Korean leader Kim Jong Un in China, a surprise announcement that could become another focal point of his visit.

Nikkei Asia is on the ground in Shenzhen to cover the meetings.

Further reading:

Here are the latest developments (Shenzhen time):

Thursday, Nov. 19

12:43 p.m. Trump met with Putin on the sidelines of the APEC forum following the plenary leaders session. Their meeting comes ahead a bilateral between Trump and Xi and a trilateral among the three leaders.

"We've had a great relationship for many years. We know each other for a long time, and I think a lot of wonderful things can come out of this, or at least start. But I think they'll come out of this," Trump told Putin.

12:35 p.m. Elon Musk told an APEC organizer that he was a "super fan" of China, according to a social media post by Yuyuan Tiantian, an account affiliated with Chinese state broadcaster CCTV.

According to the post, the Tesla and SpaceX boss told Ren Hongbin, president of the China Council for the Promotion of International Trade, about his admiration for China's "magnificent buildings and natural landscapes" as well as its railway system.

Tesla will continue to increase production in China, Musk said, according to the post. He was photographed sitting in a room across Ren, wearing a black jacket, pants and shoes.

12:06 p.m. APEC plenary session ends

10:58 a.m. Putin tells his APEC counterparts that Russia contributes to regional energy security and that they can "always count on Moscow." He also invites all regional partners to use Russian logistics infrastructure.

10:39 a.m. Trump spoke about the U.S. economy and claimed his administration is taming inflation. He also said in his remarks that trade deals were forthcoming.

"The United States has been a Pacific power for hundreds of years, and we continue to work to promote growth and stability, sovereignty, prosperity, and peace throughout this region," he said.

Trump also said AI regulation needed to be carefully managed and opposed measures that would "stifle" the industry. "We won't allow that to happen," he said.

Trump said he looked forward to meeting with Xi and Putin later this afternoon. but did not elaborate. The trilateral will follow a two-way meeting between Xi and Trump, their third this year.

10:30 a.m. Putin is taking the opportunity presented by APEC to shore up ties with Asian partners. He and Vietnamese leader To Lam agreed to step up cooperation with "a focus on traditional and new energy, including nuclear power, wind power and gas-fired power," according to Vietnam's readout.

The statement also says they "underscored the importance of maintaining peace, security and stability, increasing dialogue and cooperation, and upholding the role of multilateralism, the United Nations and the fundamental principles of international law."

10:10 a.m. In his opening address, Xi called for cooperation on Al and supply chains. The Chinese president proposed building "four key pillars" for development in the Asia-Pacific: economy and trade, connectivity, innovation and development.

He said China will provide $20 million to support cooperation in areas such as digital technology and clean energy.

9:50 a.m. Xi has opened the leaders summit, with the visiting dignitaries gathered around circular tables in a large conference room under chandeliers. Moments before sitting down for the plenary session, they took a photo with Xi in the center, flanked by Putin and Trump. Takaichi was positioned in the back row to the side.

9:40 a.m. In an interview with Fox News, Trump said he spoke with Xi about artificial intelligence, and former Nvidia chief Jensen Huang only came up "briefly," Reuters reports.

"I haven't heard that she was a spy," Trump said, in reference to Huang's extramarital affair with Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang.

9:30 a.m. APEC leaders are gathering for the forum's main event, which begins with a "family photo" before they convene for the plenary session. Xi has urged his guests to pursue "concrete results" promoting economic openness and innovation, but time is limited. Attention in the afternoon will turn to the U.S.-China bilateral meeting and the highly anticipated Trump-Xi-Putin trilateral. There are reports that Trump will squeeze in a one-on-one meeting with Putin as well, although it is unclear how substantial that would be.

9:28 a.m. While we await today's events, here's some reading. A report to U.S. Congress on Wednesday by the U.S.-China Economic and Security Review Commission said that the unusually active" level of engagement between Trump and Xi is masking Beijing's ongoing efforts to outcompete America economically, technologically and militarily.

8:00 a.m. The most anticipated day of the APEC gathering is about to unfold. Looking at Trump's schedule, he will attend an APEC Leaders' Plenary Session at 09:45 a.m., followed by a bilateral with Xi and then a trilateral with Xi and Putin. We will also be looking out for other meetings on the sidelines. The wild card could be the arrival of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, but as always information out of the Hermit Kingdom is spotty.

12:10 a.m. Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi spoke with Russian President Vladimir Putin for about 30 minutes on the sidelines of the APEC summit and related meetings in Shenzhen, their countries' first face-to-face leaders' meeting since Russia invaded Ukraine in 2022.

According to the Japanese government's account of the talks, Takaichi pressed Putin to release a Japanese journalist detained for more than a month and reverse measures putting Japan Tobacco's Russian subsidiaries under local management. The two agreed to maintain communication at various levels.

Wednesday, Nov. 18

9:20 p.m. In a welcome speech at the banquet, Xi called on APEC leaders to work toward "concrete results" when they convene Thursday morning. He said they will discuss expanding mutual openness, explore paths for innovation-driven growth and broaden opportunities for practical cooperation across various sectors, state news agency Xinhua reports.

Xi said that since his first visit to Shenzhen in 1978, the small fishing village has become a "gateway for China's high-standard opening-up."

"Openness is in Shenzhen's DNA," he is quoted as saying.

9:00 p.m. Footage and photos coming out of the APEC leaders' banquet show some highly anticipated diplomatic interactions. Trump and Putin are seen shaking hands as Xi looks on, a prelude to Thursday's closely watched trilateral summit.

Xi also is pictured shaking hands with Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi. This was a major "will they or won't they" question ahead of the summit, as China-Japan ties have been frosty for over a year, since Takaichi spoke about a potential Taiwan crisis in the Japanese parliament. Takaichi is pictured smiling broadly at Xi after the greeting.

7:00 p.m. Chinese leader Xi Jinping and his wife, Peng Liyuan, are hosting a banquet at the Shenzhen International Exchange Center for APEC leaders. Live footage from state broadcaster CCTV shows U.S. President Donald Trump arriving at the venue.

6:00 p.m. South Korean President Lee Jae Myung held talks with Chinese leader Xi Jinping earlier amid speculation that Trump could meet North Korean leader Kim Jong Un in Shenzhen.

Xi told Lee he is willing to support "various efforts aimed at easing tensions on the Korean Peninsula, including a North Korea-U.S. dialogue," according to South Korean National Security Adviser Wi Sung-lac, as quoted by the Yonhap news agency.

Lee had asked China to play "a constructive role" in addressing Korean Peninsula issues, which the South Korean president described as a "do or die" matter, according to the same Yonhap report.

Chinese state-owned news outlet Xinhua made no mention of a potential Trump-Kim summit or of Korean Peninsula tensions in its account of the meeting published Wednesday afternoon.

Xi and Lee acknowledged that next year marks the 35th anniversary of their countries' diplomatic relations. Xinhua said Xi called the anniversary an opportunity to promote the steady development of their ties. Xi also mentioned that both countries are "beneficiaries of multilateralism and free trade," poking at a possible wedge between the U.S. and its key Asian ally, given Trump's tariff policies.

Lee called for strengthening the neighbors' relations "based on the mutual trust and friendship the two countries have built so far," referring to the anniversary, according to Yonhap.

5:05 p.m. Xi greets Trump on the tarmac, reciprocating a rare airport welcome that Trump afforded him when he visited Washington in September. Ties between the rival superpowers have grown increasingly tense in recent weeks over tech restrictions and other contentious points, but the Shenzhen gathering provides the two leaders an opportunity to maintain their fragile trade truce. At the airport, the atmosphere appears friendly, with the presidents chatting and smiling before making their way past an honor guard and a welcome crew waving Chinese and American flags.

Xi stands and waves as Trump departs in his black limo, known as the Beast.

4:45 p.m. Trump lands in Shenzhen. TV footage shows Air Force One taxiing at the airport.

3:30 p.m. Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese reveals in remarks to CEOs that he spoke with Xi about his first visit to Shenzhen back in 1998, when he was a young politician. Back then, the city was still a long way away from becoming the tech hub it is today.

"You don't think of it as a same place," he said. Like Thailand's Anutin immediately before him, Albanese called Shenzhen an example of the region's success.

3:00 p.m. Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul recounts how Chinese Premier Li Qiang "kept telling me the story of Shenzhen" when they met in Bangkok on Friday, about how a fishing village four decades ago became a global business metropolis.

Anutin said he interpreted the story of the APEC host city as an example of how a "transformation can be achieved where an economy opens itself up."

The Thai leader touted the benefits of Thailand's preparations to join the Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development. "Our OECD accession process is helping improve governance and regulatory standards and transparency," he said.

Regarding online scam groups that are active especially in Thailand's border regions with Myanmar and Cambodia, Anutin stresses that there is a "global partnership" to fight cross-border organized crime.

2:15 p.m. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney tells APEC's business gathering that his country is taking "practical steps" with China on financial cooperation, including for times of stress. He also cites growing collaboration in the green economy sector, crediting China's wind and solar industries for the opportunities they create.

Carney -- whose government has faced friction with the U.S. under Trump despite the neighbors' traditionally tight ties -- has made a point this year to improve relations with China.

Praising the Chinese leadership that turned Shenzhen into a tech hub, he said, "The choices that built this city will lift this whole region." And he says that "Canada has made our choice to build a more stronger, prosperous and a more sovereign future."

Carney alluded to geopolitical tensions, saying "it's no insight to say that this has been a difficult year for international consensus." However, he said, APEC is delivering on tangible cooperation.

12:00 p.m. South Korean President Lee Jae Myung meets with Xi on the sidelines, and tells him that he wants to work together to promote peace and stability on the Korean Peninsula, according to the media pool. Xi tells his guest that he is willing to work with South Korea on preserving stable industrial supply chains.

Their meeting comes amid growing rumblings that North Korean leader Kim Jong Un could make an appearance at APEC to meet with some attendees, including Trump. U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio told reporters earlier in Manila that Trump is "serious" about engaging with Kim and "prepared to do it," although he acknowledged that a meeting might not materialize.

11:30 a.m. Russian President Vladimir Putin piles on with implicit criticism of the U.S., saying that "former dominant powers" have tried to suppress the development of other countries.

"Economic domination and coercion are now a thing of the past," he says, praising nations that have preserved their own identities and independence and arguing that sanctions and tariffs have not held Russia back.

He hails Shenzhen as a "modern vibrant megacity" and a symbol of tech, economic and social transformation in China and Asia. The region, he says, is setting an example of a "more fair, democratic and equal world order."

Putin also says he expects significant benefits from his upcoming trilateral meeting with Xi and Trump.

11:15 a.m. Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim is the next to address business leaders after China's Xi. While praising the host several times, Anwar delivers thinly veiled criticism of the U.S., without naming it directly. He stresses the importance of free and open business activity, emphasizing, "You can't say in one voice [that you're] promoting trade and investment, but only to your country."

11:10 a.m. Stan Shih, the founder of computer maker Acer and Taiwan's representative to the APEC summit, says he will "actively" engage with other members in Shenzhen as he departs from Taipei, according to Reuters.

APEC is one of the few international organizations that includes Taiwan, which participates as "Chinese Taipei." The administration is sending Shih in lieu of President Lai Ching-te, who Beijing considers a "separatist" because he rejects its territorial claim to Taiwan.

Shih describes Taiwan as a "trustworthy" player in the region and an indispensable partner for the global technology and AI sectors. He vows to "show the international community Taiwan's strength and contributions."

"Taiwan will go with a smile," he says.

10:10 a.m. Xi addresses the APEC CEO Summit, his first time to do so in person since 2018 in Papua New Guinea. Positioning himself as an advocate for stability, he called for resolving differences through dialogue and for defending free and open trade. He is discussing the dilemmas economies face between being open or closed, between cooperation and division and between change or taking a conservative approach. "These are all questions of our time that we must answer," he said.

9:45 a.m. The second day of APEC proceedings is about to get underway. Putin landed in Shenzhen overnight, while Trump is expected to fly in later in the day, as is Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi. A number of leaders, including Xi and Putin, are due to deliver speeches to business participants, with more bilateral mettings on the sidelines.

Tuesday, Nov. 17

5:30 p.m. Xi continues his day of meetings with visiting leaders, sitting down separately with Mexico's Claudia Sheinbaum, Peru's Keiko Fujimori and Chile's Jose Antonio Kast.

Mexico last year riled China by approving higher tariffs on countries with which it does not have trade deals, affecting hundreds of products. The move was widely seen as an effort to close a "back door" to the U.S.

Sheinbaum told Xi she is eager to step up cooperation with China in areas related to technology, agriculture, water, health and tourism, according to Reuters.

4:30 p.m. Speculation that North Korean leader Kim Jong Un could appear at APEC and meet with Trump continues to grow. Russia's Interfax news agency has cited the Kremlin as saying that Putin could also meet Kim if he shows up in Shenzhen, adding weight to the prospect of a Kim visit.

Shortly before he departed the U.S. for Asia, Trump himself suggested that a meeting with Kim could happen. Trump met Kim three times during his first presidency and has expressed interest in a reunion.

3:30 p.m. BYD Chairman and President Wang Chuanfu says on a panel that the electric carmaker's Thailand and Indonesia plants have created 6,000 local jobs each and nearly all of its employees at the factories are local hires.

"Our goal is not merely to export Chinese technology globally; we also aim to generate local employment and tax revenue, fostering mutually beneficial cooperation and win-win outcomes," he said.

Wang added that its Thailand factory sources just over half of components domestically.

His comments come as a rush of Chinese vehicle exports stokes trade tensions with some partner economies.

2:00 p.m. Papua New Guinea Prime Minister James Marape has assured Xi that Taiwan no longer operates in his country. PNG pushed for the closure of Taipei's representative office in its capital, Port Moresby, and Taiwan announced earlier this month that it would indeed shut down the mission.

Marape told Xi that he hopes the move "assists you in your efforts for reunification," referring to China's claim to Taiwan, which the administration in Taipei rejects.

Taiwan had been a major buyer of gas from PNG, but said it would halt spot purchases in reaction to the closure. China, in turn, committed to increasing its purchases.

12:30 p.m. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said there is now "greater predictability and stability" in his country's ties with China, as he met Chinese President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen. Xi said that since the two leaders agreed to promote a strategic partnership back in January, exchanges and cooperation between China and Canada have fully resumed.

Carney's visit to Beijing in January thawed a relationship that had been severely strained in recent years, especially after the 2018 detention of Huawei executive Meng Wanzhou in Canada and the subsequent jailing of two Canadians on espionage charges -- all of whom were eventually released.

A statement released by Carney's office about Tuesday's meeting says that Canada "has recalibrated our relationship with China -- strategically, pragmatically, and decisively." It also says the two sides agreed to extend and expand a preliminary agreement to address trade issues, opening up greater access to the Chinese market for Canada's farmers and seafood harvesters and securing more tariff relief for about 400 million Canadian dollars ($280 million) worth of exports.

The statement also mentions a slew of other initiatives to boost trade, e-commerce, educational exchanges and air travel.

11:30 a.m. Trump's Air Force One made a refueling stop in Alaska before a layover in the Philippines, where Manila is hosting ASEAN leaders and related summits.

Before leaving Washington, Trump said he might meet North Korean leader Kim Jong Un in China. The hermit nation is not a member of APEC and South Korean officials played down the possibility of such a meeting, Yonhap News Agency reported on Nov. 11.

Trump's planned attendance at APEC contrasts with last year's summit in Gyeongju, South Korea, when he met Xi Jinping in Busan and secured a trade truce but left before the main agenda began. His Shenzhen engagement signals an effort to keep ties with Xi on track ahead of next month's G20 Summit in Miami, where they are expected to meet again.

9:30 a.m. Beijing has yet to formally respond to Washington's latest move to tighten China's access to advanced artificial intelligence chips through overseas data centers. Vice Premier He Lifeng raised concerns over U.S. restrictions on China in a phone call earlier this month.

The broader AI boom is also rattling markets. Shenzhen's tech-heavy ChiNext Index sank 4.4% on Monday to a nearly 16-month low, led by steep losses among suppliers to AI data centers. U.S. stocks also fell sharply ahead of Nvidia's earnings on Tuesday.

9:00 a.m. Foreign leaders are trickling into Shenzhen. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum and Papua New Guinea Prime Minister James Marape arrived on Monday, according to Chinese media.

The leaders are expected to hold bilateral meetings with Xi on Tuesday, according to media reports. Carney is visiting China for the second time this year. In January, he met with Xi and lowered Canada's tariff wall on Chinese electric vehicles by setting up an import quota. Among the topics expected to be discussed during his visit to Shenzhen is Chinese investment into Canada's auto sector.

Trade tensions loom over Sheinbaum's visit, after she raised import tariffs on cars, textiles, appliances and other items from countries without free trade agreements with Mexico, including China. In addition to meeting Xi, she is expected to speak at the CEO Summit on Tuesday.

news.title: Relationship with China a Great One: Trump Praises Xi
news.text: Shenzhen, China: US President Donald Trump has praised Chinese President Xi Jinping's leadership and the warm reception extended to him in China, describing the relationship between Washington and Beijing as a "great one" ahead of a proposed historic trilateral meeting involving Russian President Vladimir Putin on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit.Speaking at the APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen, Trump thanked Xi and Chinese First Lady Peng Liyuan for their hospitality, describing the arrangements and reception during his visit as "unbelievable"."You've done an unbelievable job and you're an incredible leader," Trump said while praising Xi."I want to thank President Xi and Madame Peng for the incredible display they put forth.
